questions.prompt: Explicit Euler is applied to the undamped oscillator x''=-x with a fixed step h. What happens to the energy 0.5(x^2+v^2)?
options: It oscillates around the true value without drift.
It grows by the factor (1+h^2) per step.

questions.prompt: Explicit Euler on x''=-x with h=0.3. By what factor is the energy multiplied in one step? Precision 0.001.
A method has global errors 8e-3 at step h and 2e-3 at h/2 (same final time). Observed order p=log2(e(h)/e(h/2)). Precision 0.01.
questions.skillLabel: Measure the order of a method

questions.prompt: A motor model y'=-20y is simulated with explicit Euler. Largest stable step h (s)? Precision 0.001.
A pendulum swung from 1.0 rad is simulated with the small-angle model. The period is 6.6% short of the real one even when dt is made tiny. Which statement is right?
options: The error is modelling error; the integrator solves the wrong equation accurately.
The integrator is explicit Euler; switch to RK4 and the period error will vanish.
dt is still too large for the integrator; keep shrinking it until the period matches.
Float32 round-off accumulates over each cycle and is the cause of the short period.
questions.explanation: The error does not vanish with dt, so it is not discretization error.
questions.skillLabel: Separate model error from numerical error

questions.prompt: `n = int(0.3/0.1)` gives 2 in Python. Why is it a hazard for validation against an analytic solution at t=0.3?
options: It makes the energy grow, since the missing step injects extra energy each period.
It makes the integrator unstable, because the last step overshoots the stability limit.
It changes the order of the method, since the last step has a different size.
The run stops at t=0.2, so the comparison error is dominated by a wrong end time.
questions.explanation: 0.3/0.1=2.9999999999999996 truncates; use round with a divisibility check.
questions.skillLabel: Measure the order of a method

questions.prompt: You must simulate a robot hand with stiff contacts for training. Which integrator family and validation checks would you choose, and why not plain explicit Euler?
rubric: Names an implicit/semi-implicit family and links it to the stiffness stability limit h<2/lambda.
Names checks: step-size convergence study, penetration depth, energy not increasing.
Notes the trade-off between accuracy, cost and robustness (RK4 loses order at contacts).
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
